what: Two new EU AI Act prohibitions apply: systems that generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery. Machine-readable marking of synthetic output under Article 50(2) also applies to generative systems already on the market
who: Any firm offering generative AI in the EU
todo: Confirm your vendors mark synthetic output and that your own builds do too

what: FINRA's 2027 oversight report, if it follows the 2026 report's release on 9 December 2025
todo: Re-read the 2026 report's agent section and check you can track agent actions and decisions

what: Colorado's Automated Decision-Making Technology in Consequential Decisions Act takes effect, replacing the 2024 Colorado AI Act: notice before use, an explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome, and meaningful human review on request
who: Developers and deployers using automated decisions in lending, insurance, employment and other covered areas for Colorado consumers
todo: Identify which automated decisions reach Colorado consumers; deployers keep compliance records for three years after each use

what: The FCA publishes its evaluation of the second AI Live Testing cohort: Aereve, Barclays, Coadjute, Experian, GoCardless, Lloyds Banking Group (Scottish Widows), Palindrome and UBS. Testing ends by the end of 2026
todo: Read it for the supervisor's view of production AI in banking, payments and credit data

what: The US banking agencies' request for information on model risk and "banks' use of AI, including generative AI and agentic AI", promised in April when SR 26-2 left both out of scope. Not in the Federal Register as of 24 October 2026
todo: Prepare your answer now: how you validate retrieval, guardrails and agent actions, and how you would stop an agent

what: A ruling on OpenAI's and Microsoft's summary judgment motions in the news publishers' copyright cases, including New York Times v. OpenAI. The publishers filed their opposition in October 2026; no ruling date has been set
who: Anyone training or fine-tuning on third-party content
todo: Inventory the provenance of every corpus your models touch

what: The first lawsuit brought in the name of the DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, created under the executive order of 11 December 2025. The DOJ intervened on 24 April 2026 in xAI's challenge to the 2024 Colorado AI Act, which Colorado then repealed and replaced
who: Firms planning around state AI laws
todo: Avoid building compliance around any single state regime until this settles

what: General-purpose AI models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 must comply; each member state must have at least one operational AI regulatory sandbox
who: Model providers directly; firms that fine-tune or rebrand models
todo: Ask your model vendors for their compliance position and documentation

what: EU AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply, including creditworthiness and credit scoring of individuals, life and health insurance pricing, and recruitment
who: Lenders, insurers and employers using AI in the EU
todo: Start conformity and logging work now; deployers must keep logs for at least six months

what: High-risk obligations for AI built into products regulated under Annex I apply
todo: Note it; little action for most financial firms
